newsitem.title: CHINA: China to issue new futures regulations in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to issue new futures regulations in 1997.

text.p: China will issue new regulations on its futures markets next year aimed at reducing speculative trading and making information more public, the Financial News said on Saturday.
The futures department of the China Securities Regulatory Commission would issue five sets of regulations in the first half of 1997, the newspaper quoted a commission official as saying.
The new rules would include temporary regulations on futures trading and temporary regulations on the management of futures brokers, the official said.
Other regulations would cover accounting and financial matters related to futures trading, the official said but gave no further details.
The rules would include measures to curtail T+0, or same-day, settlement of futures transactions, the official said.
Every futures exchange would also be required to implement a more open information system, the official said.
Separately, the securities commission would also explore ways to merge some of China's 14 futures exchanges or link them electronically, the official said but did not elaborate.
Industry officials have said there are too many exchanges and that their number eventually might be reduced to four or five.
